sections.h2: What is Royse City and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Royse City is on State Highway 66 about five miles northeast of Rockwall, in the northeastern corner of Rockwall County, and parts of it lie in Collin and Hunt Counties as well. That three-county layout is the first thing to understand before you sell.

According to the Texas State Historical Association, the town was named for G. B. Royse, who platted the townsite in 1886, and settlement began in 1885 when the Missouri, Kansas and Texas Railroad was planned through the area. Early residents and businesses moved over from nearby Fate, which the railroad bypassed. By 1890 the community had about 1,000 people, two cotton gins and a gristmill. It was first incorporated in 1891, voted out in 1902 and reinstated in 1906.

The population stayed near 1,000 to 2,000 for most of the twentieth century and reached 2,957 in 2000. The city's recent budgets show much faster growth in taxable value, which is why houses here now trade in a market shaped by newer subdivisions around older downtown blocks.

sections.h2: Why does it matter that Royse City sits in three counties?
sections.html:
It determines which appraisal district values your house and which county clerk records your deed. The city's budget says the Rockwall, Collin and Hunt County appraisal districts each certify values for property inside the city, and Rockwall CAD compiles the three rolls.

Look at the top of your tax statement or search each district's property search to find the right one. An exemption must be applied for with each appraisal district in which the property sits.

sections.h2: What are your options for a fast sale in Royse City?
sections.html:
You can list, sell for cash, or sell to a renovator. The best choice depends on whether the house is move-in ready and how soon you need funds.

  • List with an agent: best when the house is clean and in good repair, with the longest timeline.
  • Cash offer: shortest timeline and fewer contingencies, usually at a lower price.
  • Renovator sale: suits houses with older systems, damage or a hard-to-sell layout.

Newer subdivisions around Royse City often have homeowners association rules, so ask the association for a resale certificate or dues statement early, since the title company will need it.

sections.h2: Do you need a permit in Royse City before selling?
sections.html:
No permit is needed to sell, but the city says building permits must be obtained before any improvement or alteration to a property. If you have finished a project, such as a pergola, flatwork or electrical change, confirm it was permitted.

  • Permits, contractor registration, fee payment and project status run through the city's MyGov system.
  • Plan review can take up to 10 business days, with feedback through MyGov or email.
  • Contractors must be registered before they can get a permit.
  • Inspection requests must be in by 4 pm for next-day inspection.

The Building Inspection department can be reached at 972-524-4710 or permits@roysecity.com.

sections.h2: How do property taxes and exemptions work when you sell in Royse City?
sections.html:
Texas sets the calendar: values are set January 1, bills go out around October 1, and tax is late after January 31. The homestead appraisal cap limits yearly value increases on a residence homestead to 10 percent, starting the year after the exemption is first qualified.

Statewide, school districts must give a $140,000 residence homestead exemption, and a homeowner 65 or older or disabled gets an additional $60,000 school exemption plus a school tax ceiling. A buyer who moves in after January 1 can get the exemption for the rest of the year if the prior owner had none. Ask the appraisal district for your property's current exemptions, since county and city amounts vary.

The state also lets any owner with a homestead exemption pay in two halves, with the first due by November 30 and the second by June 30. If a closing falls between those dates, the title company will confirm what is paid.

sections.h2: What if the house has a lien, a tenant or an estate?
sections.html:
Each situation has its own deed and filing rules.

  • Tax lien: the January 1 lien secures that year's tax, so unpaid tax follows the property and must be cleared before closing.
  • Tenant: an eviction starts with a written notice to vacate, usually at least three days, then a justice court suit, with appeal due within five days of judgment.
  • Estate: inherited houses may pass by transfer on death deed, a court-approved muniment of title, an affidavit of heirship or an administrator's deed.

Recording happens at the county clerk where the land sits, so a Royse City house may be recorded in Rockwall, Collin or Hunt County. The clerk manual lists $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page.

faqs.q: Which county do I pay taxes to for a Royse City house?
faqs.a: It depends on where the parcel sits. The city lies partly in Rockwall, Collin and Hunt Counties, and each county's appraisal district certifies values within the city.

faqs.q: Does Royse City require permits for fences or flatwork?
faqs.a: The city has guides for flatwork and for arbors, pergolas and gazebos, so call 972-524-4710 before assuming no permit applies.

faqs.q: How long does Royse City plan review take?
faqs.a: Up to 10 business days, according to the city, with feedback sent through MyGov or by email.

faqs.q: Can heirs sell a Royse City house without probate?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A transfer on death deed recorded before the owner's death passes property without probate, and otherwise a muniment of title or affidavit of heirship may apply. A title company will state which one a buyer's lender will accept.
After January 31, according to the Texas Comptroller. A six percent penalty and one percent interest are added on February 1.
